name: PIK3CA mutation
summary: Activating PIK3CA mutations are among the most common alterations in hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative breast cancer and predict benefit from PI3K-alpha and AKT pathway inhibitors combined with endocrine therapy.
biology: PIK3CA encodes p110alpha, the catalytic subunit of class IA PI3K, which generates PIP3 to activate AKT and mTOR, driving growth, survival and metabolism. Hotspot mutations in the helical domain (exon 9) relieve inhibition by the p85 regulatory subunit, and kinase-domain mutations (exon 20) increase membrane association. Crosstalk with ER signalling contributes to endocrine resistance.
alterations: Other activating mutations (e.g. N345K, C420R), including multiple-in-cis mutations

testing.specimen: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumour tissue (primary or metastatic) or plasma ctDNA
testing.notes: PIK3CA mutations are usually truncal and stable; a negative plasma result should be followed by tissue testing if feasible.

predictiveRelevance: PIK3CA mutation predicts benefit from alpelisib plus fulvestrant after endocrine therapy, inavolisib plus palbociclib and fulvestrant in endocrine-resistant disease, and capivasertib plus fulvestrant (selected on PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN alterations).
resistance: Insulin feedback-driven PI3K reactivation (hyperglycaemia-induced insulin release)
